claims.text: The two characters `#!` at the very start of a file, followed by a path, make the system run the program at that path and hand it the file; bash then reads the remaining lines in order, one at a time.
claims.source_hint: Bash Reference Manual, 'Shell Scripts' (3.8); C# language reference, preprocessor directives (#! and /usr/bin/env)

claims.text: `#!/usr/bin/env bash` starts `bash` through `env`, which finds it wherever the machine keeps it instead of the file naming one fixed folder.
claims.source_hint: C# language reference, preprocessor directives (`/usr/bin/env` locates the executable in PATH); GNU Coreutils manual, 'env'

claims.text: `set -e` makes bash exit as soon as a command ends with a status other than 0.
claims.source_hint: Bash Reference Manual, 'The Set Builtin', -e / errexit; GitHub Actions workflow syntax, jobs.<job_id>.steps[*].shell (default bash flags, -e described)

claims.text: `set -u` makes bash treat the expansion of a variable that was never set as an error instead of an empty value.
claims.source_hint: Bash Reference Manual, 'The Set Builtin', option -u / nounset

claims.text: `set -o pipefail` makes a pipeline count as failed when any command in it fails, instead of taking the status of its rightmost command only.
claims.source_hint: Bash Reference Manual, 'The Set Builtin', pipefail; GitHub Actions workflow syntax, jobs.<job_id>.steps[*].shell (pipefail described)

claims.text: `${1:-/tmp/backups}` expands to `$1` when it is set and not empty, and to `/tmp/backups` otherwise.
claims.source_hint: Bash Reference Manual, 'Shell Parameter Expansion', ${parameter:-word}; Dockerfile reference, 'Environment replacement' (names it a standard bash modifier)

claims.text: The shell splits what it reads into words at the spaces between them, so a path typed unquoted becomes two arguments; double quotes, whether typed or written around `"$1"`, prevent that splitting and keep the value one argument.
claims.source_hint: Bash Reference Manual, 'Word Splitting', 'Double Quotes' and 'Shell Operation' (tokenisation)

claims.text: Every command leaves an exit status behind: 0 means it did what it was asked, any other number means it did not.
claims.source_hint: Bash Reference Manual, 'Exit Status'; GitHub Actions workflow syntax, run steps (non-zero exit code fails the step)

claims.text: `$?` expands to the exit status of the most recently executed foreground command, so it reports on that one command only.
claims.source_hint: Bash Reference Manual, 'Special Parameters', $?

claims.text: `a || b` runs b only when a exited non-zero and `a && b` runs b only when a exited 0; `set -e` does not exit for a command that is part of such a list unless it is the last one.
claims.source_hint: Bash Reference Manual, 'Lists of Commands' (&& and ||) and 'The Set Builtin', -e exceptions

claims.text: A script exits with the status of the last command it executed.
claims.source_hint: Bash Reference Manual, 'Exit Status'; exit builtin

claims.text: `$1` and `$2` are the first and second words written after the script's name, `$0` is the path of the script itself, and `$@` is all of its arguments.
claims.source_hint: Bash Reference Manual, 'Positional Parameters' and 'Special Parameters' ($0, $@)

claims.text: `[ -f path ]` exits 0 when path exists and is a regular file, and non-zero otherwise.
claims.source_hint: Bash Reference Manual, 'Bash Conditional Expressions', -f; test builtin

claims.text: The lab box is the box `scripts/up.sh` starts; the file `/.dockerenv` is present inside it and absent on the machine that starts it, which is what line 5 of the script tests, and the dump is written inside the box.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang at stage-0: scripts/up.sh, docker-compose.yml (repo mounted read-only), scripts/lab-run.sh, STAGE.md lab box section; Docker docs on the container filesystem

claims.text: `exec` replaces the running shell with the named program rather than starting it as a child, so nothing of the original run continues afterwards; here the same file starts again from its first line inside the lab box.
claims.source_hint: Bash Reference Manual, 'Bourne Shell Builtins', exec; examples/don-hang at stage-0 (scripts/lab-run.sh)

claims.text: A `\` at the end of a line joins it to the next, so lines 11 and 12 are one command; `>` sends that command's standard output into a file instead of to the screen, while what it writes as a complaint still reaches the screen.
claims.source_hint: Bash Reference Manual, 'Escape Character' (line continuation) and 'Redirecting Output' (file descriptor 1 only)

claims.text: `$( … )` runs the command written inside it and substitutes what that command printed on standard output.
claims.source_hint: Bash Reference Manual, 'Command Substitution'

claims.text: `pg_dump --schema-only` writes the object definitions — which tables exist and what each one holds — without any of the rows; `--host`, `--username` and `--dbname` name the database, and `--no-owner --no-privileges` leave ownership and grants out of the dump.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 documentation, pg_dump reference: options --schema-only, --no-owner, --no-privileges, --host, --username, --dbname

claims.text: The dump of the Đơn Hàng database at stage-0 holds six `CREATE TABLE` lines, so line 15 of the script prints 6.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang at stage-0: db/schema.sql and outputs/stage-0/scripts/terminal/backup-db.txt

claims.text: Line 18 prints 0 after every run because `$?` there holds the status of the `echo` on line 17, which was given nothing to print, so it printed the blank line in the output and succeeded; that 0 is not `pg_dump`'s status.
claims.source_hint: Bash Reference Manual, 'Special Parameters' $? and 'echo' builtin (no operands); outputs/stage-0/scripts/terminal/backup-db.txt at stage-0

claims.text: Running `scripts/terminal/backup-db.sh /tmp/mine` makes the script's first printed line read `wrote /tmp/mine/donhang-schema.sql`, with the same table count as a run without an argument.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang at stage-0: run scripts/terminal/backup-db.sh with one argument and compare with outputs/stage-0/scripts/terminal/backup-db.txt

claims.text: Whatever starts a script reads the exit code it leaves rather than the words it printed: the shell here, and elsewhere the program that runs a build or deployment step, which is why reading such a step starts with reading a script.
claims.source_hint: GitHub Actions documentation, 'Workflow syntax', run steps and their exit status

claims.text: `dirname` prints the folder part of the path it is given, so `dirname "$0"` names the folder the running script sits in whenever the script was started by a path that includes that folder.
claims.source_hint: GNU Coreutils manual, 'dirname: Strip last file name component'; Bash Reference Manual, 'Special Parameters', $0

claims.text: `mkdir -p` creates the folder and any missing folder above it, prints nothing, and ends with 0 when the folder is already there instead of failing.
claims.source_hint: GNU Coreutils manual, 'mkdir: Make directories', option -p / --parents
